Hi Alex / Lydia — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps: 

- Scope: real-time triage assistant for intake forms (~350 tokens per request, peak concurrency ~60-80)
- Redwood ask: provide representative sample traffic and a preferred success metric (p99 latency under 120ms, and median under 45ms)
- Our commit: run a short in-house bench with a model variant that matches your throughput targets and share results + config suggestions by EOD tomorrow

Action items for us: Marissa will run the bench and send over the readout + recommended kv-cache and batching settings. Action items for Nimbus: if you can share a small trace/example file (synth or redacted) it speeds validation — optional but helpful.

If the numbers look good we can set up a 30-min technical review next week to align on rollout timelines. Is Wednesday (Aug 25) morning PT good for you?

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Post-demo: latency numbers and next steps — bench readout attached

Alex / Lydia — following up with the bench run I promised. High-level summary up front:

- Test config: 8x A10G, model X-small-quant (8-bit), sequence length 400, KV cache enabled, batching tuned for p99 target
- Observed: median token latency ~32ms, p50 request latency ~48ms, p99 request latency ~118ms under a sustained 60-concurrency synthetic workload (350 token payloads)
- Notes: tail increases when concurrency spikes past 90; enabling prefix caching for repeated prompts reduced p99 by ~20% in our tests

Attaching two artifacts: nimbus_latency_readout.pdf (charts + raw numbers) and kvcache_config.txt (the config snippet we used). The PDF includes the exact harness commands and request timing distribution.

If you want, we can rerun with a model variant that trades off a few points of quality for reduced tail latency — happy to show that delta.

Connor — flagging the recommended follow-up: 30-min tech sync to go over the PDF and decide whether to trial Dedicated pool for a smoke test.

Thanks,
Marissa
